newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian car tariffs should drop - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian car tariffs should drop - report.

text.p: Australia's Industry Commission said on Friday it believed tariff assistance for the domestic automotive industry should be reduced to five percent by 2004.

In a draft report on the industry, the commission said two of its commissioners believed tariffs on cars and parts should be reduced by 2.5 percentage points each year until 2004 when it will reach the general rate for manufacturing of five percent.

"(Presiding commissioner Bill) Scales said that this would be consistent with APEC commitments and would place Australia in a good position to achieve the APEC goal of free trade by 2010," the commission said in the report.

The report said Webber, former managing director of Chrysler Australia Ltd and director of its successor Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd, believed a further review was necessary around 2000 and that it should consider the industry's viability at the time as well as other APEC countries' progress in reducing tariffs.
The report also said the industry was concerned about the effects of taxation on the demand for vehicles and about slow progress with infrastructure reform
"The commission endorses the industry's call for fundamental tax reform and for more rapid microeconomic reform," it said.
Australia's car makers are subsidiaries of General Motors Corp, Ford Motor Co, Mitsubishi Motors Corp and Toyota Motor Corp.
